summary: Shoppers first settle whether the laptop's USB-C port carries video and how many added screens the laptop can run, then choose freestanding or attached, and only then compare size, resolution, touch and price; ChatGPT asked the port question in 6 of 6 chats. Freestanding monitors are a price fight that Arzopa leads today ($92.13 for 144 Hz, $117.79 for 2560×1600, $132.98 for Wired's 180 Hz best overall), so the products we link place on layout and fit lines (stacked, attached, two screens on a Mac, driver-free, detachable), not on price lines. In the last 60 days ASUS's ZenScreen OLED MQ16FC reached $199 on Amazon, a 15.6-inch 1080p monitor hit $39, and Mobile Pixels' and FOPO's store prices moved (Float 2 Pro $247.99, Trio 3 Pro $407.99, FOPO 16-inch three-panel $599.99 with the 14-inch at $499.99).

axes.label: Whether the laptop's port can send video to the screen, and whether a driver is needed
axes.why: ChatGPT raised it in 6 of 6 chats ("Does your laptop's USB-C port support video output?"). Kotaku's deal write-up of 2026-11-27 states one USB-C cable carries power and video only if the device supports DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt 3. Mobile Pixels sells the Duex DS on USB-C plus Mini HDMI "without the need for drivers or software".

breakpoints.value: USB-C with DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt
breakpoints.why: One cable carries power and video; without it the screen needs HDMI plus separate power, or a driver-based link.
Xebec's store says its $59 Tri-Screen 3 Mac Adapter "is required for all Mac users", so a single-cable claim does not hold on a Mac without it.

axes.label: How many screens are added: one, two or three
axes.why: ChatGPT asked "one added screen or two?" in 2 of 6 chats and told shoppers to check the laptop's external-display limit, particularly on a Mac. Our best-for page on triple extenders for the MacBook Air drew 6 visits, the most of any single page type here.

breakpoints.why: Apple's tech specs for the MacBook Air (M2, 2022) list "One external display"; a second added screen on it needs a driver-based link.
Apple's tech specs for the MacBook Air (13-inch, M4, 2025) list "Up to two external displays", so two added screens can run with no driver if each has its own video-capable port.

rules: A screen extender attaches to the laptop lid; a portable monitor stands on its own. Every page states how many screens are added, because 'triple' means two added screens on some listings and three panels on others (FOPO S788, S980). The first question is the video path: one cable works only from a USB-C port with DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt; otherwise HDMI plus separate power, or a driver. On a Mac, Apple's tech-specs page for the exact model decides how many added screens run without a driver (MacBook Air M2: one; 13-inch M4: two), and Xebec's store says its adapter is required on every Mac. Prices count only from the maker's US store or the Amazon listing on the day; Arzopa's Z3FC read $31.44 on Amazon on 2026-11-27, which is not usable. Brightness, sRGB and weight are maker figures unless a named tester measured them: Wired measured sRGB and watts; RTINGS ranks brightness but hides its numbers. Weights with and without stand or cover are not comparable (ViewSonic TD1656-2K: 1.8 lb bare, 2.8 lb with stand, 2.92 lb at Wired with cover). All URLs here were opened 2026-11-27; Wired, RTINGS and the Glance page were read through a reader proxy.

pages_to_fix.why: Our research angle prices the 16-inch FOPO S788 at $499.99 ($166.66 a screen). Today $499.99 is the 14-inch variant; the 16-inch is $599.99, or $540.00 with code FOPO. Correct any $499.99 on the page.

The Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro is $407.99 today, above the page's limit. Two-screen units under $400 today are FOPO S11 ($399.99, $360.00 with code), S9G and S10 ($299.99, $270.00) and S7 ($199.99, $180.00).
No reviewer, standard or search suggestion read draws a line at 2 lb; Wired only says to consider weight. The figure is a round number, and weights with and without stand or cover are not comparable.
$250 is not among the price tiers Google completes for portable monitors (50, 100, 150, 200). Extender-specific price suggestions were not read, so confirm before keeping the number.

If the page recommends the Fold 15.6 ($143.99) as a freestanding screen, Arzopa's Z3FC ($132.98, Wired's best overall) and Z1RC ($117.79, 2560×1600) beat it on figures at this price. Keep the page to attached extenders or say so.
Same check: the Fold 16 QHD ($167.99) has the Z1RC's resolution for $50 more and 220 cd/m², and an ASUS OLED is $199.00.
15.3 inches at 1920×1200 is one product's panel (FOPO S980), not a figure shoppers were found to decide on; the page has 0 visits.
Price check only: the Duex Float 2 Pro is $247.99 today, against $263.49 in Mobile Pixels' 2026-11-02 post.

espresso Pro 15 and Lite 15 prices at the maker's US store (store address returned 404); both are left out of the field.
Today's prices for LG gram +view 16, Lenovo ThinkVision M14, ViewSonic VA1655, MSI Pro MP165 E6, Elecrow CrowView Note and ASUS ZenScreen Duo OLED MQ149CD.
Battery monitors beyond Elecrow and Pixcase: UPERFECT and ASUS battery models were not opened, and the Amazon search returned untitled listings.

ASUS MQ16FC size (press release says 16-inch, Amazon title 15.6 inch), brightness, weight and US launch date.

FOPO S780, S780C/S788C and the generic triple product: specs, driver and whether code FOPO applies; Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS price today (last read 2026-11-21 at $215.99).
